definition: PhyCV is the first computer vision library which utilizes algorithms directly derived from the equations of physics governing physical phenomena.
details: The algorithms appearing in the first release emulate the propagation of light through a physical medium with natural and engineered diffractive properties followed by coherent detection. Unlike traditional algorithms that are a sequence of hand-crafted empirical rules, physics-inspired algorithms leverage physical laws of nature as blueprints. In addition, these algorithms can, in principle, be implemented in real physical devices for fast and efficient computation in the form of analog computing. Currently PhyCV has three algorithms, Phase-Stretch Transform (PST) and Phase-Stretch Adaptive Gradient-Field Extractor (PAGE), and Vision Enhancement via Virtual diffraction and coherent Detection (VEViD). All algorithms have CPU and GPU versions. PhyCV is now available on GitHub and can be installed from pip.

explainer.lead: PhyCV is a computer vision library whose algorithms are derived directly from physics equations rather than hand-crafted empirical rules. It matters because it offers a different, physically grounded blueprint for vision algorithms.

tiers.eli5: Instead of teaching a computer a long list of if-then rules for seeing, PhyCV uses the same math that describes how light moves through water or glass.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use PhyCV algorithms that emulate light propagation through diffractive media followed by coherent detection; a pitfall is assuming these physics-derived algorithms behave like conventional empirical pipelines. In principle the algorithms can be implemented in real physical devices for analog computation.
tiers.paperLevel: PhyCV algorithms are derived from equations governing physical phenomena, emulating light propagation through a medium with natural and engineered diffractive properties followed by coherent detection; the approach is limited to phenomena describable by those physical laws.

explainer.example: A PhyCV edge-detection routine simulates light passing through a diffractive medium and then coherent detection to produce an output image.
